Let the rate be \(R\%\) per annum and the sum be \(P\).

Simple interest for 2 years:
\[
\frac{2PR}{100}=10200
\]
\[
\frac{PR}{100}=5100
\]

Compound interest for 2 years:
\[
P\left[\left(1+\frac{R}{100}\right)^2-1\right]=11730
\]
\[
P\left[\frac{2R}{100}+\left(\frac{R}{100}\right)^2\right]=11730
\]

Using \( \frac{PR}{100}=5100 \):
\[
2(5100)+P\left(\frac{R}{100}\right)^2=11730
\]
\[
P\left(\frac{R}{100}\right)^2=1530
\]

Since \(\frac{R}{100}=\frac{5100}{P}\):
\[
P\left(\frac{5100}{P}\right)^2=1530
\]
\[
\frac{5100^2}{P}=1530
\]
\[
P=\frac{5100^2}{1530}=17000
\]

\[
\boxed{17000}
\]
